Among 70 non-MPR patients in `mmc5.csv`, 64 had non-missing Texp and recurrence-free survival data. Using the median non-MPR Texp value (`Texp.in.Tex.relevant*10 = 8.052753644`) to define high vs low Texp, 32 of 64 analyzable non-MPR patients were high Texp, i.e. 50.0% (or 32/70 = 45.7% of all non-MPR patients if those with missing Texp are kept in the denominator).

These high-Texp non-MPR patients had substantially more favorable recurrence-free survival despite lacking pathological response: 12-month KM RFS 90.2% vs 58.2%, 24-month KM RFS 86.4% vs 41.6%, log-rank p = 0.000391, and Cox HR for recurrence = 0.174 (95% CI 0.059-0.519, p = 0.00171) for high vs low Texp.

Therefore, approximately half of analyzable non-MPR patients have high Texp cell levels, and this subgroup shows favorable recurrence-free survival despite non-MPR status.
